check: whether the 23 never-executed GameTests will actually be discovered and scheduled by the pending run
why: Establishing that 23 tests have never run is only useful if they will run next time. A class can exist, compile and be registered yet still never execute if the framework does not schedule it - and that failure is silent, which is the shape this session has already found twice.
allSixClassesAreRegistered: BiomeWriterGameTests, LifecycleGameTests, NegotiatedGateGameTests, PaletteGameTests, SiteRuntimeIndexGameTests and WallArchPreparationGameTests all appear in fabric.mod.json's fabric-gametest entrypoint list, which holds 35 entries.
noneCarriesABatchAttribute: Checked each class for a batch attribute and found none, so every one of their tests falls into defaultBatch rather than a named batch that might not be scheduled.

batchAccountingReconciles.namedBatches: 33 across 13 batches - pgw-allocation-audit 7, pgw-cold-allocation 7, pgw-adjacency-decision 6, pgw-adjacency-fixture-diagnostic 3, pgw-adjacency-matrix 2, and one each for pgw-ground-portals, pgw-tall-columns, pgw-production-memory, pgw-hydro-boundary, pgw-curved-gate-regression, pgw-survival-matrix, pgw-curve-matrix and pgw-curved-site-matrix

theTwentyThreeAreInsideDefaultBatch: Their six classes contribute 3, 3, 3, 4, 7 and 3, which is 23, and all sit within the 96. So the batch that runs by default is the batch that carries them.
conclusion: No configuration is needed. The pending run will execute all 23 as part of defaultBatch, and the results.xml check of 129 entries against six named classes remains the way to confirm it happened.
whatThisRulesOut: The failure mode where a class is registered but its tests are never scheduled - checked for by confirming both the entrypoint registration and the batch assignment, rather than assuming registration implies execution.
